newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-JUVENTUS MOVE TOWARDS FINAL WITH WIN AT AJAX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS MOVE TOWARDS FINAL WITH WIN AT AJAX.

text.p: Champions Juventus moved to within sight of the European Cup final with a disciplined 2-1 win away against Ajax Amsterdam in the first leg of their semifinal on Wednesday.
Ajax managed to prevent a demolition job by the Italians, who destroyed AC Milan 6-1 at the weekend, and scored what may prove to be a vital second half goal.
But the Dutch champions could not stop the tie, a replay of last year's final, going to Juventus again.
Ajax now have an uphill task, knowing they need to score at least twice in Turin.
The match was played in front of a capacity 51,000 crowd including Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and some 2,500 supporters who had made the journey from Turin.

Ajax began well, attacking down the flanks through Marc Overmars and Nigerian international Tijani Babangida, but Juventus, playing a flat back four marshalled by the dominant Ciro Ferrara, were rarely troubled.
But Juve, tight in defence then swift on the counter, lived up to their pre-match billing. Ajax's Finnish striker Jari Litmanen last week called them the best club side in the world.

In the 14th minute a Juventus counter involving Italy's new international Christian Vieri and France's Zinedine Zidane undid the Ajax defence and found Nicola Amoruso on hand at the edge of the six-yard box to slot the ball home.

Juve's second goal in the 41st minute again involved a quick break from defence. This time, France's Didier Deschamps found Vieri with enough space on the edge of the penalty area to fire a well-placed shot beyond the diving grasp of Edwin van der Saar.

For all the good work in the first half by Overmars and Babangida, Ajax sorely missed the central target of Patrick Kluivert, who underwent a knee operation earlier on Wednesday which was expected to keep him out for up to six weeks.

In the second half, the Ajax defence continued to struggle with the omnipresent Vieri but in the 66th minute Ronald de Boer threaded a pass through to Litmanen, who with only keeper Angelo Peruzzi to beat, kept his cool to score.

The goal lifted Ajax, but it was too little too late and the Dutch side, already unlikely to win any domestic silverware, face a tough return leg in the cavernous 69,000 seater Delle Alpi stadium in Turin on April 23.
Ajax coach Louis van Gaal said Juventus were as good as he had expected.
"(Juventus) were a fantastic team. They all worked for each and they seem to have the time to make the right choices," he said.
Midfieder Richard Witschge also acknowledged the Italian's strength. "They were superior, tactically very strong," he said.
Juventus coach Marcello Lippi's only problem appears to be the loss of Vladimir Jugovic for the second leg. The Yugoslav international picked up his second yellow card of the tournament.
